title: Neoantigen & Personalized Peptide Vaccine Atlas - RTK II Glioblastoma
case: Adult, age 48; GBM IDH-wildtype methylation class RTK II; 1.2 cm lesion gross-totally resected; treatment-naive; newly diagnosed
scope: Worldwide. Section 1: institutional trials of a personalized neoantigen vaccine (peptide/mRNA/DNA/dendritic-cell), personalized peptide selection (PPV), or closely related shared-antigen peptide vaccine, open or landmark. Section 2: private/commercial providers selling this outside a registered trial.

section1_open_trials.name: ZSNeo-DC1.1 — neoantigen-pulsed dendritic-cell vaccine + temozolomide
section1_open_trials.molecular_hla_fit: IDH1/IDH2 wild-type explicitly required — the one trial here whose molecular criterion directly matches this case. MGMT not restricted. Needs sufficient tumour + blood for neoantigen identification and adequate venous access for PBMC collection.
section1_open_trials.tissue_needed: Adequate banked tumour tissue for sequencing/neoantigen identification required. Confirm what was preserved from the 1.2 cm resection.
section1_open_trials.timing_window: Enrol after surgery and after completing standard concurrent chemoradiation — a more forgiving timeline than the pre-chemoradiation vaccine trials, because the vaccine is given during adjuvant temozolomide.
section1_open_trials.manufacturing: Neoantigen identification from tumour + blood before randomisation; manufacturing time not stated (DC products typically 3–6 weeks after apheresis).
section1_open_trials.fit_rationale: Best molecular match on paper (IDH-wildtype required), randomised with a proper control, vaccinates in the adjuvant window so it does not compete with the Stupp protocol. Against it: not yet open (planned start Jan 2026), sponsor and contact are China-based so likely China-only sites — international enrolment and tissue logistics would be the hard part.
section1_open_trials.evidence_note: Early-stage platform: a phase 1b of ZSNeo-DC in newly diagnosed GBM (NCT04968366) and a recurrent-glioma trial (NCT06253234, recruiting) precede this randomised phase 2; no glioblastoma survival data are published yet.
key_inclusion: Age 18–75; histologically confirmed newly diagnosed glioblastoma (WHO grade 4)
IDH1/IDH2 wild-type
Post-surgery and standard concurrent chemoradiation completed
KPS 50–100; life expectancy >3 months
Sufficient tumour/blood for neoantigen identification; adequate venous access for PBMC collection
key_exclusion: Prior interventional trial within 4 weeks; carmustine wafers within 6 months
Active autoimmune disease or systemic immunosuppression within 30 days
Active HIV / hepatitis B / hepatitis C / syphilis
Uncontrolled cardiovascular, metabolic or systemic disease
section1_open_trials.secondary_endpoints: Overall survival; survival rates; disease control / best overall response / clinical benefit rate; investigator-assessed PFS; safety.
section1_open_trials.dates: Planned start Jan 2026 · primary completion Dec 2028
flags: Not yet recruiting; sites not posted — likely China-only. Contact the sponsor to ask about international patients and whether tissue can be shipped.

section1_open_trials.name: PTPRZ1 / TERT peptide vaccine, adjuvant to chemoradiation
section1_open_trials.sponsor: Assistance Publique – Hôpitaux de Paris (PI A. Carpentier)
section1_open_trials.molecular_hla_fit: Histologically confirmed glioblastoma; IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma excluded (so IDH-wildtype fits). Phase 1 requires HLA-A2 positive and PTPRZ1 expression in the tumour. Retrospective TERT-promoter and MGMT testing on archival tissue. Steroids must be <=10 mg/day prednisone-equivalent.
section1_open_trials.tissue_needed: Standard archival tissue is sufficient for the required biomarker testing.
section1_open_trials.timing_window: Starts 28–45 days after chemoradiation completion — adjuvant window, no conflict with the Stupp protocol.
section1_open_trials.manufacturing: Off-the-shelf peptides against two glioma-associated antigens (PTPRZ1, TERT) — no per-patient synthesis; "personalisation" is by HLA type and antigen expression.
section1_open_trials.fit_rationale: Open now, adjuvant-window, and standard archival tissue is enough — practically the easiest European entry to screen for. Two gates: HLA-A2 positivity and PTPRZ1 tumour expression (Phase 1 cohort), and travel to Paris or Marseille. It targets shared antigens, not the patient's own mutations.
section1_open_trials.evidence_note: TERT is the target of the UCPVax telomerase-vaccine programme, which has phase 1/2 immunogenicity and some efficacy signal in other settings; this specific PTPRZ1/TERT construct is first-in-human in GBM.
key_inclusion: Age 18–75; histologically confirmed glioblastoma
Concurrent radiotherapy (≥45 Gy) + temozolomide completed 28–45 days earlier
KPS ≥60%
Phase 1 only: HLA-A2 positive and PTPRZ1 tumour expression
Archival tumour available for TERT-promoter and MGMT testing
key_exclusion: Autoimmune disease (lupus, RA, IBD); systemic immunosuppression
Prior bevacizumab or VEGF antagonist; carmustine wafers
section1_open_trials.primary_endpoint: Phase 1: maximum tolerated dose / recommended phase 2a dose. Phase 2a: anti-TERT-specific T-cell response at 2 months.
section1_open_trials.secondary_endpoints: Immunological safety; anti-PTPRZ1/anti-TERT T-cell evolution; PFS (RANO 2.0); overall survival; quality of life; cardiac safety.
flags: Phase 1 cohort needs HLA-A2 positivity and PTPRZ1 expression — confirm both before travelling.
Shared-antigen vaccine, not built from the patient's own neoantigens.

section1_open_trials.name: Autologous dendritic cells loaded with autologous tumour homogenate
section1_open_trials.molecular_hla_fit: Histologically confirmed monofocal glioblastoma. Near-complete resection (<=5 mL residual tumour) required — matches a gross-total resection. IDH/MGMT not restricted. Steroids must be <=10 mg prednisone-equivalent.
section1_open_trials.tissue_needed: Fresh viable tumour for homogenate preparation, plus leukapheresis. Confirm fresh tissue was banked.
section1_open_trials.manufacturing: Dendritic cells (10×10⁶/dose) loaded with a homogenate of the patient's own tumour — whole-tumour antigens, not a defined neoepitope list. Needs fresh tumour + leukapheresis.
section1_open_trials.fit_rationale: Its resection and steroid criteria fit this patient well, and it is open to any IDH/MGMT status. Against it: a single Italian centre, small, and the registry primary-completion date has passed — confirm it is still enrolling before counting on it. Whole-tumour DC vaccine, not neoantigen-defined.
section1_open_trials.evidence_note: DC + tumour-lysate/homogenate vaccines have a long phase 1/2 track record in GBM with occasional survival signals but no positive randomised trial (DCVax-L remains contested).
key_inclusion: Age ≥18; histologically confirmed monofocal glioblastoma
Near-complete resection (≤5 mL residual tumour volume)
KPS ≥70% or ECOG 0–1; life expectancy >12 weeks
Suitable for leukapheresis (negative HIV/HBV/HCV/syphilis)
key_exclusion: Active autoimmune disease treated within 2 years
Other malignancy within 5 years (minor skin/cervical in situ exceptions)
section1_open_trials.secondary_endpoints: In vivo immune response; overall survival; HLA class I/II characterisation.
section1_open_trials.dates: Started Mar 2025 · primary completion listed Jul 2025 (verify current status)
flags: Registry primary-completion date has passed — confirm the trial is still open before contacting.
Single centre, Italy; needs fresh tumour tissue.

section1_open_trials.name: Hybrid allogeneic-DC × autologous tumour-cell fusion vaccine ± pembrolizumab
section1_open_trials.sponsor: University of São Paulo General Hospital (PI J.A.M. Barbuto)
section1_open_trials.molecular_hla_fit: Histological glioblastoma with confirmed IDH status; undergoing or completed standard of care; tumour cells must be expandable in culture. No upper age limit; performance score >50.
section1_open_trials.tissue_needed: Needs viable tumour cells that can be culture-expanded — fresh tissue from the resection. Confirm availability.
section1_open_trials.manufacturing: Allogeneic dendritic cells from healthy donors fused with the patient's own tumour cells — needs a viable tumour cell culture. Personalized by the autologous tumour half.
section1_open_trials.fit_rationale: A properly controlled, blinded phase 3 — the most rigorous design in this atlas — and open to any IDH/MGMT status with no age cap. Against it: not yet open, Brazil-based, and it needs a living tumour cell culture, which is often not available after a small completed resection unless specifically set up.
section1_open_trials.evidence_note: The São Paulo group has prior phase 1/2 experience with DC-tumour fusion vaccines; this is the first phase 3 of the approach.
key_inclusion: Adult (≥18, no upper limit); histological glioblastoma, IDH status confirmed
Undergoing or completed standard surgery + chemoradiotherapy
Performance score >50; able to attend follow-up every 2 months
Tumour cells capable of culture expansion
section1_open_trials.secondary_endpoints: Progression / survival metrics; quality of life; immunological response; safety.
section1_open_trials.contact: Prof. José Alexandre Marzãgão Barbuto · +55 11 3091-7375 · jbarbuto@icb.usp.br
section1_open_trials.dates: Planned start Jan 2026 · primary completion Jan 2028
flags: Needs a viable tumour cell culture — usually must be arranged at surgery.

section1_open_trials.name: Tamavaq™ — AI-designed personalized neoantigen + tumour-antigen peptide vaccine
section1_open_trials.molecular_hla_fit: Registry inclusion text describes recurrent malignant glioma with prior surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy, a measurable lesion (RECIST), high mutation load (>10 TMB) and >=10 neoantigens, >=3 months post-op, no prior immunotherapy — despite the study title saying "newly diagnosed".
section1_open_trials.tissue_needed: Tumour tissue for sequencing and neoantigen identification.
section1_open_trials.timing_window: Tied to a maintenance-temozolomide cycle; not a fixed post-op window.
section1_open_trials.manufacturing: 1–35 synthetic neoantigen peptides selected by a proprietary "AI-QMMM" pipeline, plus a large fixed panel of GBM-associated antigens (MAGE-1, HER-2, gp100, survivin, EphA2, IL13Rα2, others), with a rotating menu of adjuvants (poly-ICLC, cGAMP, GM-CSF, imiquimod, CpG, MPLA, saponins).
section1_open_trials.fit_rationale: Serious mismatches for this case: the eligibility text is written for recurrent, measurable disease and demands a high mutational burden (>10 TMB, ≥10 neoantigens) that a treatment-naïve, fully-resected RTK II tumour is unlikely to meet; the title and criteria contradict each other; it is a single small-company site with a pharmacist PI and an unusually broad multi-adjuvant design. Worth noting, not pursuing without direct clarification.
section1_open_trials.evidence_note: First-in-human; no efficacy data. Sponsor has limited clinical track record.
key_inclusion: Age ≥18; histologically confirmed glioma
Recurrent malignant glioma; prior surgery / radiotherapy / chemotherapy
High mutation load (>10 TMB); genetically unstable; ≥10 neoantigens
Measurable lesion per RECIST; KPS >60; estimated survival >3 months
No prior immunotherapy
key_exclusion: Prior immune checkpoint inhibitor or experimental immunotherapy
Active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment
Uncontrolled cardiovascular/metabolic disease; HIV; active hepatitis B/C
section1_open_trials.primary_endpoint: Safety; adverse / serious adverse event incidence; MRI monitoring.
section1_open_trials.secondary_endpoints: RANO / Macdonald response; advanced MRI and PET; circulating tumour DNA; T-cell immune analysis; survival.
flags: Eligibility text is recurrent-disease and high-TMB oriented — contradicts the "newly diagnosed" title. Clarify directly before considering.
Single small-company site; first-in-human; broad unproven multi-adjuvant design.

section1_landmark_not_enrolling.name: NeoVax — personalized neoantigen peptide vaccine + radiotherapy + pembrolizumab
section1_landmark_not_enrolling.sponsor: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute / Massachusetts General Hospital
section1_landmark_not_enrolling.evidence_note: Keskin et al., Nature 2019 (n=8): 6/8 dexamethasone-free patients generated polyfunctional neoantigen-specific CD4+/CD8+ T cells that trafficked into the tumour; dexamethasone abrogated responses; no serious toxicity; no survival claim. Updated at ASCO 2026 (Reardon et al., abstract 2006): vaccine-stimulated anti-tumour immune activity still evident in some patients at 1 year, and survival extended vs historical observations for similar patients — uncontrolled, not a randomised comparison.
section1_landmark_not_enrolling.why_listed: Not enrolling. This is the reference platform — the version every peptide entry in this atlas is measured against — so it is here for its data and as the group most likely to open a successor. Ask the Dana-Farber Center for Neuro-Oncology what is next.

section1_landmark_not_enrolling.name: GAPVAC-101 — APVAC1 + APVAC2 fully personalized peptide vaccine
section1_landmark_not_enrolling.sponsor: DKFZ / DKTK, Heidelberg & Tübingen (led by W. Wick)
section1_landmark_not_enrolling.evidence_note: Hilf et al., Nature 2019 (n=15 vaccinated): median PFS 14.2 months and median OS 29 months from diagnosis; APVAC1 drove sustained central-memory CD8 responses, APVAC2 predominantly CD4. Proof of concept for fully personalized vaccination; not powered for efficacy.
section1_landmark_not_enrolling.why_listed: Completed after a 16-patient feasibility cohort with no confirmatory trial to follow. The same Heidelberg group defined the RTK II methylation class this whole dashboard is built around, so this is the most directly relevant lineage — but there is nothing to enrol in. It also feeds the German private route (see CeGaT in Section 2).

section1_landmark_not_enrolling.name: XS15-adjuvanted multipeptide vaccination + standard chemoradiation
section1_landmark_not_enrolling.evidence_note: Completed phase 1; immunogenicity read-out with XS15 as a strong T-cell adjuvant. No efficacy claim.
section1_landmark_not_enrolling.why_listed: Completed in 2024. Restricted to MGMT-methylated, HLA-A2-positive patients. Listed because it is the academic backbone of the Tübingen peptide-vaccine ecosystem that also runs the CeGaT private route in Section 2.

section1_landmark_not_enrolling.name: Personalized genomic (neoantigen) vaccine + Tumour Treating Fields
section1_landmark_not_enrolling.sponsor: Adilia Hormigo (Albert Einstein College of Medicine, Bronx NY; now also Mount Sinai)
section1_landmark_not_enrolling.evidence_note: SNO abstracts (CTIM-17, CTIM-10): treatment well tolerated with induction of robust epitope-specific T-cell responses; formal survival read-out not yet published.
section1_landmark_not_enrolling.why_listed: Not enrolling (enrolment ran Dec 2017–Jul 2020, n=13). Included because it is a distinct US personalized-neoantigen GBM programme, notable for pairing the vaccine with Tumour Treating Fields, and because the investigator (Hormigo) is active at Albert Einstein / Mount Sinai — a group to watch for a successor.

appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.status_setting: Randomised phase 2b, newly diagnosed; data cut-off Jul 2026, readout pending
appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.reported: Phase 2a: 1-yr OS 93.7%, median OS 25.9 mo; phase 2b passed interim futility
appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.relevance: Survivin is broadly expressed regardless of methylation subclass; the most advanced shared-antigen peptide vaccine in newly diagnosed GBM. Already covered on the main dashboard.
Same antigen/product as above, earlier cohort.

appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.reported: Phase 1 immunogenicity; multi-antigen to reduce escape
appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.relevance: A multi-peptide shared-antigen design that tries to avoid rindopepimut's single-antigen failure mode.

appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.reported: No overall-survival benefit; recurrences were EGFRvIII-negative (antigen escape)
appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.relevance: Directly cautionary for RTK II: EGFRvIII is common here, but a single-antigen EGFRvIII peptide vaccine did not work. ⚠

appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.antigen: Bacterial "OncoMimic" peptides of IL13Rα2, survivin/BIRC5, FOXM1
appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.status_setting: Phase 1b/2a completed; recurrent / first-progression GBM; MGMT-methylated patients eligible
appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.where: US (incl. Dana-Farber), France, Germany, Spain — Enterome
appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.reported: n=100; EO2401 + nivolumab +/- bevacizumab; SNO 2025 cohort-3 survival signal; sponsor says a randomised trial is warranted
appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.relevance: A shared-antigen peptide vaccine that is open to MGMT-methylated disease. Recurrent-only and completed - a "for later" option, not a first-line one; watch for the randomised follow-up.

appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.reported: 87% immune response; favourable outcomes in IDH-mutant astrocytoma
appendix_shared_antigen_peptide_vaccines.relevance: Not applicable — this patient is IDH-wildtype. Listed so the distinction is explicit.

section2_private_providers.name: Jaime Leandro Foundation (JLF) — expanded-access neoantigen synthetic long peptide vaccine
section2_private_providers.location: US 501(c)(3); administrative sites in Miami FL, Dallas TX, St Louis MO, Los Angeles & San Francisco CA. Expanded-access (JLF-100) treating site on the registry: Texas Oncology, Austin TX. Basket trial (JLF-200) sites incl. Miami Beach FL, Beverly Hills & San Francisco CA, New York NY, Bridgeton MO.
section2_private_providers.contact_website: Jaime Leandro Foundation for Therapeutic Cancer Vaccines (501(c)(3), USA). Web: jaimeleandrofoundation.org · Email: info@jaimeleandrofoundation.org (William Hoos) · Enrolment infrastructure: WideTrial (widetrial.com). Administrative sites: Miami FL, Dallas TX, St Louis MO, Los Angeles CA, San Francisco CA (per the foundation; no street addresses published - contact by email). Expanded-access (JLF-100 / NCT06963697) treating site on the registry: Texas Oncology - Central Austin, 6204 Balcones Dr, Austin, TX 78731 · Tel +1 512-451-4411 · PI Brian Vaillant, MD. Basket trial (JLF-200 / NCT05741242, enrolling by invitation) sites: Mount Sinai Comprehensive Cancer Center, Miami Beach, FL (this is Mount Sinai Medical Center Florida, not the New York Mount Sinai); Precision NextGen Oncology, Beverly Hills CA; Quest Clinical Research, San Francisco CA; Anna Gattani MD PC, New York NY; St Louis Cancer Care, Bridgeton MO. Registries: NCT06963697 · NCT05741242.
section2_private_providers.what_is_manufactured: Personalized neoantigen synthetic long peptides (8-35 amino acids), a customised mix per patient based on the tumour's mutation profile, given with poly-ICLC adjuvant - the same class of product as NeoVax.
section2_private_providers.starting_material: The patient's tumour + matched normal for exome/RNA sequencing and neoepitope prediction; blood for HLA typing.
section2_private_providers.what_is_offered: An FDA expanded-access programme (individual + intermediate-size patient population; NCT06963697 / protocol JLF-100), run by a US non-profit whose stated mission is to make personalized cancer vaccines available to patients with limited or no options. It is not a clinical trial you enrol in for research - it is treatment access under 21 CFR 312.305, alongside the foundation's phase 1b/2 basket trial JLF-200 (NCT05741242).
section2_private_providers.personalized: Fully personalized - built from the patient's own tumour mutations.
section2_private_providers.peptide_synthesis: GMP synthetic long peptide manufacturing (contracted); a bioinformatics neoepitope pipeline (the foundation has published its ImmunoNX workflow).
section2_private_providers.combination: Poly-ICLC adjuvant; other therapy at the treating physician's discretion.
section2_private_providers.regulatory_framework: FDA expanded-access IND. Eligibility (21 CFR 312.305, treating-physician judgement): unable to enrol in the JLF-200 trial; has received or is ineligible for FDA-approved therapies for that cancer; estimated 5-year survival <50%. Condition on the record is "cancer / local or metastatic solid tumours" - glioblastoma is neither named nor excluded; the listed site PI (Brian Vaillant, MD) is a neuro-oncologist, so CNS tumours appear to be in scope - confirm directly.
section2_private_providers.cost_headline: ≈ USD 83,000 for the vaccine series (self-pay cost recovery, reported)
section2_private_providers.est_cost: Not stated on the ClinicalTrials.gov record. STAT News (2023) reported ~USD 83,000 for the vaccine series, via a WideTrial cost-recovery arrangement (FDA permits cost recovery for expanded access). Get the current figure and what it covers in writing.
section2_private_providers.insurance: Self-pay; expanded-access cost recovery is not billable to insurance. The foundation is a 501(c)(3) and describes the programme as self-pay compassionate use.
section2_private_providers.evidence: No published glioblastoma outcomes. The foundation reported treating its first patient (2023) and runs the parallel JLF-200 basket trial; efficacy data for the peptide platform in GBM specifically were not located. First-in-class for most indications.
section2_private_providers.patient_story: The foundation's site (jaimeleandrofoundation.org) carries news of its first treated patient; no independently verified GBM outcome accounts.
section2_private_providers.logistics: US-based (Austin, TX listed); self-pay; requires a treating physician willing to hold/participate in the expanded-access IND and to certify 21 CFR 312.305 eligibility.
section2_private_providers.what_is_unverified: Independent scrutiny exists: STAT News framed the ~USD 83,000 charge for an unproven vaccine critically. This is a legitimate FDA pathway, but it is still an investigational product with no efficacy proof, and GBM eligibility is not spelled out on the record - verify scope, current cost, the manufacturing/QC package, and how many patients have been treated before committing.

section2_private_providers.name: Immunocine Cancer Center
section2_private_providers.location: US administrative office: Houston, TX · treatment: Cancún & Cabo San Lucas, Mexico (an Arizona tumour-preservation service was announced in 2026)
section2_private_providers.contact_website: Immunocine Cancer Center. Web: immunocine.com (enquiry form at immunocine.com/contact) · Tel: +1 346-214-9142 · Email: Amcfarlane@immunocine.com (Amy McFarlane, communications) · US administrative base: Houston, TX · Treatment clinics: Cancún and Cabo San Lucas, Mexico · Facebook: facebook.com/Immunocine.
section2_private_providers.what_is_manufactured: Autologous monocyte-derived dendritic cells exposed ex vivo to "tumour-specific antigens" and re-infused, made in a cGMP lab (per the company). Not a defined-neoepitope product - no ranked neoantigen list is published.
section2_private_providers.starting_material: The patient's own tumour tissue (preserved at the Arizona intake site) plus blood / leukapheresis for monocytes.
section2_private_providers.what_is_offered: Autologous dendritic-cell immunotherapy for many cancers including glioblastoma: the patient's monocyte-derived dendritic cells are exposed to "tumour-specific antigens" and re-infused. A US (Arizona) site handles tumour preservation and intake; the cell product is manufactured and given in Cancún.
section2_private_providers.personalized: Personalized to the patient's own tumour material, but not a defined-neoantigen vaccine — it is a tumour-lysate / tumour-antigen-pulsed DC product. The company does not publish a per-patient neoepitope list.
section2_private_providers.peptide_synthesis: Cell product (cGMP lab, per the company); no per-patient peptide synthesis.
section2_private_providers.combination: Marketed as a stand-alone DC vaccine; details of any adjuvant/checkpoint pairing not published.
section2_private_providers.regulatory_framework: US site provides preservation/intake services only; the cellular treatment is delivered in Mexico, outside FDA oversight.
section2_private_providers.est_cost: Not itemised publicly; secondary sources put personalized DC immunotherapy of this kind at roughly USD 50,000. Request a full written quote including the US intake fees and the Cancún treatment.
section2_private_providers.insurance: Not billed to US insurance; treatment is in Mexico. Superbill / receipts only; out-of-network reimbursement not guaranteed.
section2_private_providers.evidence: No peer-reviewed glioblastoma outcome data located; company press material and testimonials only.
section2_private_providers.patient_story: Company-published written and video testimonials on immunocine.com - not glioblastoma-specific, not independently verified.
section2_private_providers.logistics: US intake, Mexico treatment; self-pay; no insurance billing pathway.
section2_private_providers.what_is_unverified: Whether the "tumour-specific antigens" are defined neoepitopes or whole-tumour lysate is not disclosed; no GBM survival data; treatment happens outside the US. Ask for the antigen-selection method and GBM-specific outcomes in writing.

section2_private_providers.name: Williams Cancer Institute
section2_private_providers.location: Beverly Hills, CA & Miami, FL, USA (also a site in Mexico) — Dr Jason R. Williams
section2_private_providers.contact_website: Williams Cancer Institute (Dr Jason R. Williams). Web: williamscancerinstitute.com (consultation request on the site) · Tel: +1 863-451-9755 · Email: info@williamscancerinstitute.com · Beverly Hills: 9777 Wilshire Blvd, Suite 1004, Beverly Hills, CA 90212 · Miami: 150 SE 2nd Ave, Unit 1002, Miami, FL 33131 · also a site in Mexico · hours Mon-Fri 8a-5p CT.
section2_private_providers.what_is_manufactured: No ex-vivo product. The "vaccine" is the patient's own tumour ablated in situ (pulsed electric field / cryoablation) plus intratumoral checkpoint and cytokine injections - a different technique from a peptide/mRNA neoantigen vaccine.
section2_private_providers.starting_material: The tumour in situ; no tissue is harvested for manufacturing and no sequencing-based neoepitope selection is done.
section2_private_providers.what_is_offered: Intratumoral immunotherapy with pulsed-electric-field (PEF) ablation and cryoablation, marketed as "turning the tumour into a personalized cancer vaccine" (in-situ vaccination) plus intratumoral checkpoint and cytokine injections.
section2_private_providers.personalized: In-situ approach — it relies on antigens released by ablating the patient's own tumour. It is not a tumour-sequenced neoantigen peptide/mRNA vaccine and involves no ex-vivo peptide manufacturing.
section2_private_providers.peptide_synthesis: n/a — no peptide synthesis; the "vaccine" is the ablated tumour in situ.
section2_private_providers.combination: Intratumoral anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4, IL-2, and other agents; systemic low-dose combinations.
section2_private_providers.regulatory_framework: US site operates as practice-of-medicine with off-label intratumoral drug use; some protocols delivered at the Mexico site.
section2_private_providers.cost_headline: Self-pay; not publicly itemised — request a quote
section2_private_providers.est_cost: Not publicly itemised; self-pay. Request an itemised quote per protocol.
section2_private_providers.insurance: Self-pay; no insurance billing pathway described.
section2_private_providers.evidence: Case reports and conference material; no randomised or GBM-specific peer-reviewed outcome data located. Brain tumours are rarely the marketed indication (mostly accessible solid tumours).
section2_private_providers.patient_story: Clinic-published patient videos / testimonials (williamscancerinstitute.com) - not glioblastoma-specific, not independently verified.
section2_private_providers.logistics: Las Vegas or Mexico; self-pay; travel for repeated ablation sessions.
section2_private_providers.what_is_unverified: Included only to be explicit that this well-known US "personalized cancer vaccine" marketing is in-situ ablation, a different technique from the neoantigen peptide vaccine this atlas is about. No GBM efficacy data.

section2_private_providers.what_is_manufactured: NeoVax: up to ~20 GMP synthetic long peptides + poly-ICLC (Catherine Wu / David Reardon, Dana-Farber). Albert Einstein / Mount Sinai (Adilia Hormigo): personalized synthetic long peptides + poly-ICLC, given with Tumour Treating Fields (OpenVax neoepitope pipeline). Mount Sinai also has the PGV-001 multi-peptide neoantigen platform (Nina Bhardwaj) - after a 13-patient phase 1 across other cancers, a newly-diagnosed-GBM PGV-001 trial is planned (no registry number yet; watch Mount Sinai Tisch). Fred Hutchinson: a personalized neoantigen synthetic long peptide platform (currently melanoma / breast / lung, not GBM).
section2_private_providers.starting_material: Tumour + matched normal (blood) for whole-exome / RNA sequencing and HLA typing; requires adequate banked tumour tissue.
section2_private_providers.what_is_offered: This is the answer to "why isn't Dana-Farber / Mass General / Brigham & Women's (or Mount Sinai) listed as a provider?" - these centres run real personalized-neoantigen GBM programmes, but only as clinical trials, never as a purchasable service. The Boston GBM trial is NeoVax (NCT02287428, sites = Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Massachusetts General Hospital; Brigham & Women's is a site for the separate melanoma NeoVax, not this one; it also covers residual / progressive low-grade glioma). Albert Einstein / Mount Sinai (Hormigo) ran a personalized genomic vaccine + TTFields phase 1 (NCT03223103, n=13). All are active, not recruiting. The Washington University / Geneos Therapeutics GNOS-PV01 DNA-vaccine programme enrols MGMT-unmethylated GBM only, so it has been removed from this atlas per case direction. See the landmark section.
section2_private_providers.peptide_synthesis: GMP peptide manufacturing within each academic programme.
section2_private_providers.combination: Pembrolizumab (NeoVax); Tumour Treating Fields + temozolomide (Einstein / Mount Sinai).
section2_private_providers.regulatory_framework: FDA IND; clinical trial only. No named-patient / expanded-access neoantigen vaccine is offered at these centres - for the US expanded-access route see the Jaime Leandro Foundation entry above.
section2_private_providers.cost_headline: Trial — no charge for the investigational product
section2_private_providers.est_cost: Trial — no charge for the investigational product.
section2_private_providers.insurance: Trial - the investigational product is provided at no cost; standard-of-care items are billed as usual.
section2_private_providers.evidence: NeoVax GBM: Keskin et al., Nature 2019 (neoantigen-specific intratumoural T cells; no survival claim); ASCO 2026 update (Reardon - activity still evident at 1 year, survival extended vs historical, uncontrolled). Einstein / Mount Sinai: SNO abstracts - well tolerated, robust epitope-specific T-cell responses; survival data immature.
section2_private_providers.patient_story: No clinic testimonials; see the published / presented trial reports (Keskin, Nature 2019; Reardon, ASCO 2026; Hormigo, SNO CTIM abstracts).
section2_private_providers.logistics: Contact each centre's neuro-oncology programme about NeoVax / genomic-vaccine successor trials and timing.
section2_private_providers.what_is_unverified: Nothing to purchase here. The point of this row is that the US centres' neoantigen GBM work is trial-only and currently between studies - watch for a NeoVax or genomic-vaccine successor.

section2_private_providers.name: CeGaT GmbH / cecava GmbH
section2_private_providers.contact_website: CeGaT GmbH / CeCaVa GmbH & Co. KG (Center for Cancer Vaccines; JV with B. Braun), Paul-Ehrlich-Straße 23, 72076 Tübingen, Germany. Web: cegat.com · cecava.com · Tel: +49 7071 565 44 55 · Email: info@cegat.de · Vaccine / expanded-access enquiries: Dr Saskia Biskup, Saskia.Biskup@humangenetik-tuebingen.de · registry NCT05356312.
section2_private_providers.what_is_manufactured: GMP synthetic peptides spanning the patient's predicted neoepitopes, formulated with adjuvant - the "printing" step done with identity/purity/sterility release testing. ~12 weeks from diagnostics.
section2_private_providers.starting_material: Tumour tissue (FFPE or fresh) + blood, for tumour-exome sequencing, HLA typing and neoantigen prediction (CancerNeo®).
section2_private_providers.what_is_offered: A fully personalized neoantigen synthetic-peptide vaccine. CeGaT's CancerNeo® runs tumour-exome + HLA typing + neoantigen prediction; cecava manufactures and administers the peptide vaccine. Manufacturing ~12 weeks after diagnostics.
section2_private_providers.personalized: Fully personalized — built from the patient's own tumour mutations.
section2_private_providers.peptide_synthesis: GMP peptide synthesis (in-house / contracted); this is the "printing" step done properly, with release testing.
section2_private_providers.combination: Given with adjuvant; some patients also receive checkpoint inhibitors and immune monitoring, arranged case by case.
section2_private_providers.regulatory_framework: Legal in Germany as an individual named-patient treatment (individueller Heilversuch). Not an EMA marketing authorisation and not an efficacy approval. NCT05356312 is CeGaT's own expanded-access registry listing.
section2_private_providers.est_cost: Reported in case accounts: ~€10,000 neoantigen diagnostics; ~€39,000 vaccine; ~€3,000 immune monitoring (one family cited ~£30,000 for the peptides). Totals vary; get an itemised quote.
section2_private_providers.insurance: German statutory insurance rarely covers it; private German insurers sometimes reimburse partially, case by case. Not billed to non-German (e.g. US) insurance.
section2_private_providers.evidence: 173-patient real-world series (Nature Communications 2024): median OS 31.9 months from diagnosis across all vaccinees (70 vaccinated before progression, 103 after); patients with multiple vaccine-induced T-cell responses 53 months vs 27 months for none/low (P=0.03); vaccine-induced immune response in 87/97 (90%) monitored; adverse events mostly grade 1–2.
section2_private_providers.patient_story: Named-patient accounts appear in UK press and fundraising coverage (e.g. Brain Tumour Research features); the provider does not host a testimonial page. Outcomes in those accounts are not independently verified.
section2_private_providers.logistics: Self-pay, single centre, repeated travel to Tübingen. Easier if your oncologist co-manages; CeGaT will also work with patients directly.
section2_private_providers.what_is_unverified: An independent Neuro-Oncology 2025 commentary ("Lessons ignored?") argues the survival figures are inflated by selection bias (65% of patients KPS 90–100; international travel required; median 10.4 months from diagnosis to vaccination → lead-time bias; median follow-up only 21.3 months), uncontrolled external comparators, non-prespecified immune-response criteria, incomplete adverse-event reporting, and that 19 of 50 authors are affiliated with the provider. The number of patients sequenced but never vaccinated is not reported. No randomised data.

section2_private_providers.name: Hallwang Private Oncology Clinic

section2_private_providers.what_is_manufactured: Not disclosed for the peptide component. Broad personalised-oncology menu also includes dendritic-cell, NK and T-cell products and off-label drug combinations; the peptide-vaccine methodology is not published.
section2_private_providers.starting_material: Blood and/or tumour material, varies by protocol (not independently confirmed).
section2_private_providers.what_is_offered: Lists personalized peptide vaccines among a broad personalised-oncology menu (also dendritic-cell, NK, checkpoint, off-label combinations).
section2_private_providers.personalized: Claimed personalized; methodology not independently documented.
section2_private_providers.peptide_synthesis: Not disclosed; peptide source not specified.
section2_private_providers.regulatory_framework: German individual healing attempt. No insurance contracts of any kind (clinic states this explicitly).
section2_private_providers.est_cost: Documented cases ~USD 100,000–127,000 for a 1–3-week programme; ~80% deposit required upfront.
section2_private_providers.insurance: Clinic states plainly it has no contracts with any statutory or private health insurer; costs are settled directly by the patient, with ~80% due upfront. No billing pathway offered.
section2_private_providers.evidence: No peer-reviewed glioblastoma outcome data; the clinic does not publish survival data.
section2_private_providers.patient_story: Clinic-published testimonials (hallwang-clinic.com/en/experiences) - not glioblastoma-specific, not independently verified. GoFundMe banned Hallwang fundraisers in 2019.
section2_private_providers.what_is_unverified: Independent reporting (Science-Based Medicine and others) has specifically named this clinic for selling unproven, ineffective therapies alongside legitimate-sounding ones; GoFundMe banned Hallwang fundraisers in 2019. Also catalogued on the main dashboard's private-provider list. Scrutinise closely.

section2_private_providers.what_is_offered: IO-Vac® autologous dendritic-cell vaccine matured with oncolytic Newcastle disease virus — not a peptide/neoantigen vaccine. Listed for cross-reference only.
section2_private_providers.personalized: Personalized (autologous tumour lysate + own dendritic cells).
section2_private_providers.peptide_synthesis: n/a — cell product, no peptide synthesis.
section2_private_providers.regulatory_framework: German individual healing attempt / hospital exemption.
section2_private_providers.cost_headline: ≈ €65,000 for the first two cycles + mandatory diagnostics
section2_private_providers.est_cost: ~€23,000–26,000 per vaccination cycle; ~€65,000 for the first two cycles plus mandatory diagnostics.
section2_private_providers.insurance: German statutory insurance rarely covers it without dispute; private German insurers sometimes reimburse partially. Not billed to non-German insurance.
section2_private_providers.evidence: Single-institution case series in IDH-wildtype GBM reporting improved OS vs historical published data (PMC 2023); not randomised.
section2_private_providers.patient_story: None currently listed by the institute.
section2_private_providers.what_is_unverified: Covered in full on the main dashboard. Included here only to be clear it is a DC vaccine, not the peptide/neoantigen modality this atlas is about.

section2_private_providers.name: NEO CLINIC TOKYO
section2_private_providers.contact_website: NEO CLINIC TOKYO, 6F LB Building, 3-14-4 Shirokanedai, Minato-ku, Tokyo 108-0071, Japan. Web: neoclinic-en.jp (English) · Tel: +81 3-6450-4796 · contact form on the site.

section2_private_providers.starting_material: Tumour tissue for NGS-based mutation calling + blood; specifics (fresh vs archival, tumour-content threshold) not published.
section2_private_providers.what_is_offered: A neoantigen peptide vaccine and, separately, an "oncoantigen" (shared tumour-antigen) peptide vaccine, marketed as part of a "precision medicine" package "appropriately combined with other treatments".
section2_private_providers.personalized: Claimed personalized — NGS-based mutation calling. Number of peptides, prediction method and manufacturer not published on the English site.
section2_private_providers.peptide_synthesis: Not disclosed whether peptides are made in-house or contracted.
section2_private_providers.combination: Combined with unspecified other therapies at the clinic's discretion.
section2_private_providers.regulatory_framework: Japan free-market medicine (jiyū shinryō) under the Act on the Safety of Regenerative Medicine — a safety notification framework, not an efficacy review.
section2_private_providers.cost_headline: Not published — self-pay; request a full itemised quote
section2_private_providers.est_cost: Not published — request a full itemised quote. Japanese neoantigen/DC peptide services are typically fully out of pocket and not covered by Japanese or foreign insurance.

section2_private_providers.name: Personalized Peptide Vaccination (PPV) — Kurume University lineage / Brightpath Biotherapeutics
section2_private_providers.contact_website: BrightPath Biotherapeutics Co., Ltd. (formerly GreenPeptide), Kojimachi Central Building 7F, 2-2-4 Kojimachi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 102-0083, Japan (R&D at Kawasaki King Skyfront). Web: brightpathbio.com/english · contact form on the site. Historical PPV delivery: Kurume University Hospital, 67 Asahi-machi, Kurume, Fukuoka 830-0011 · Tel: +81 942-35-3311 (main). Also Yamaguchi University Hospital (Ube, Yamaguchi).
section2_private_providers.what_is_manufactured: Classic PPV: 2-4 pre-manufactured shared-antigen peptides selected per patient from a fixed ~30-peptide pool, given with an adjuvant. Brightpath's fully personalized neoantigen successor is still in development.
section2_private_providers.starting_material: Blood only in classic PPV - HLA-A typing plus measurement of pre-existing peptide-specific IgG to pick the 2-4 peptides. No tumour sequencing.
section2_private_providers.what_is_offered: PPV: a fixed pool of ~30 mostly shared tumour-antigen peptides, from which 2–4 are chosen per patient by HLA-A type and pre-existing peptide-specific IgG. Delivered historically through Kurume University's cancer-vaccine clinic and affiliated centres on a research / advanced-medical-care basis; Brightpath now runs the commercial and neoantigen-successor programmes (with the National Cancer Center Japan).
section2_private_providers.personalized: Per-patient selection from a shared pool — not built from the patient's own mutations. A fully personalized neoantigen successor is in development.
section2_private_providers.peptide_synthesis: Pool peptides pre-manufactured; no on-demand per-patient synthesis in the classic PPV method.
section2_private_providers.combination: Often with low-dose chemotherapy or checkpoint inhibitors in trials.
section2_private_providers.regulatory_framework: Advanced Medical Care / research framework in Japan; not funded by national insurance for general use.
section2_private_providers.cost_headline: ≈ ¥44,000–66,000 per antigen; full-course price not itemised
section2_private_providers.est_cost: Historically ~¥44,000–66,000 per antigen in the advanced-medical-care setting; total course cost not publicly itemised.
section2_private_providers.insurance: Advanced Medical Care / research setting; not funded by Japan's national insurance for general use; not covered by foreign insurance.
section2_private_providers.evidence: Two decades of Japanese phase 1/2 work across many cancers, including limited glioma. Multiple randomised phase 2/3 trials in other tumours (e.g. castration-resistant prostate, biliary tract) were negative for overall survival. No positive randomised GBM data.
section2_private_providers.logistics: Access is mostly through Japanese academic centres; ask Brightpath about current routes.
section2_private_providers.what_is_unverified: The classic PPV method has largely failed its controlled trials elsewhere; applicability to newly-diagnosed IDH-wildtype GBM is unproven. The neoantigen successor has no GBM data yet.

section2_private_providers.cost_headline: No purchasable programme in the region
section2_private_providers.evidence: None for a South American GBM neoantigen-vaccine service. The Brazilian Phase 3 (NCT06749925) has no results yet.
section2_private_providers.logistics: n/a. If pursuing the Brazilian trial once it opens, contact the University of São Paulo General Hospital neuro-oncology programme (see the Section 1 card for NCT06749925).
section2_private_providers.what_is_unverified: Regional clinical-trial registries are less complete than ClinicalTrials.gov; a small hospital-based programme could exist without an English-language footprint. Nothing verifiable surfaced. If the user has a specific centre in mind, name it and it can be checked directly.
